solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's enumeration wrong at 24 across, recounted from the answer here

clue.text: Appear when old man's out of bed?

parts.note: 'old man' is slang for father, here POP; the 's is read as 'is'
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Dad will show up once he has got out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop up is a phrasal verb meaning to turn up or arrive unexpectedly.

clue.text: Strips and endlessly sleeps around

indicators.note: turned around, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without its end, so the last letter of the word sleeps is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A promiscuous stripper who sleeps around without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' removes the final S of SLEEPS, leaving SLEEP; 'around' then rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Peels as a verb means removes the outer layer, the same action as strips.

clue.text: Might it be breakfast time in prison?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: oat ..., a breakfast dish
second meaning: British slang for a prison sentence

explanation.walkthrough: Doing porridge is British slang for serving a prison term, popularised by the 1970s sitcom of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a hot oat cereal eaten in the morning and, in slang, a stretch served behind bars.

clue.text: Quite mean to trap Republican

indicators.note: the first word holds the second inside it, as if catching it

parts.note: mean in the sense of small-minded is petty

explanation.surface: A spiteful plan to ensnare a Republican politician.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, pretty means fairly or rather, as in 'pretty good', a synonym of quite.

clue.text: Disagreeable old duke promises to pay

parts.note: IOUs (I owe you) are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: An unpleasant aged aristocrat who settles his debts with promissory notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repellent, a stronger synonym of disagreeable.

clue.text: It runs round tree, as dog does

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the outer covering wrapped round a trunk
second meaning: a dog's ... is the sound it makes

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a dog chasing round a tree, but the first half describes the tree's outer skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word is both the woody outer layer of a trunk and the sharp cry a hound gives.

clue.text: Gangster with a gun making you scared

parts.note: Al Capone, the archetypal gangster, gives AL
someone with a gun is armed

explanation.surface: A mobster with a firearm would frighten anybody.
explanation.walkthrough: AL stands for Al Capone, the Chicago gangster of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarmed means frightened or anxious, a straightforward synonym of scared.

clue.text: Children's author had a droll disposition

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A writer for the young who had an amusing temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' reads as temperament but signals rearranging HAD A DROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl wrote Charlie and the Chocolate Factory and Matilda, classic books for young readers.

clue.text: Grant wangled coke somehow

indicators.note: done somehow or other, so the letters come out in some new order

explanation.surface: A man named Grant has wangled himself some cocaine by some means.
explanation.walkthrough: Grant looks like a man's name but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a point is to concede or admit it, which is what acknowledge means.

clue.text: Creepy sounding place for a bird

indicators.note: the word is said aloud, giving another word of the same sound

parts.note: creepy means eerie

explanation.surface: A spooky-sounding spot where a bird roosts.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is the high nest of an eagle or other bird of prey.

clue.text: One critical of Her Majesty going on strike

indicators.note: the second piece is attached onto the end of the first

parts.note: to strike is to knock
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A detractor of the Queen who is taking industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going on strike' looks like a walkout, but the phrase splits: strike is the verb meaning hit, and 'going on' attaches the royal abbreviation to its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A knocker is informal for a persistent critic, someone who runs things down.

clue.text: Struck son with glove

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
a mitten is a kind of glove

explanation.surface: A boy was hit with a glove, as in a challenge to a duel.
explanation.definitionFit: Smitten is the old past participle of smite, so it means hit, as well as infatuated.

clue.text: Dirty old boy identified, you say

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word sounds like another

parts.note: identified, in the sense of spotted, is seen

explanation.surface: A grubby former pupil has been recognised, according to you.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means indecent or lewd, the smutty sense of dirty.

clue.text: Bill hiding in skip — such a lark!

indicators.note: concealed inside, so the first piece goes within the other

parts.note: to skip is to get away, escape
a bill is an advertisement, AD

explanation.surface: A poster hidden in a rubbish skip makes for a bit of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is a British large open bin for rubbish, but here it is the verb meaning to run off.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous adventure, a prank or lark.

clue.text: Track that POW might make?

indicators.note: the letters could be made into something new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A prisoner of war might wear a path while pacing.
explanation.definitionFit: A towpath is the path beside a canal or river along which horses towed barges.

clue.text: On top of everything as a rule

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in addition to all else, taken as a whole
second meaning: generally, in most cases

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase but splits into two adverbial senses of the one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall as an adverb means both in total, all things considered, and generally, much as 'as a rule' does.

clue.text: Sheep found under tree in Hindu retreat

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece lying under another comes after it

parts.note: an ash is a tree
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep sheltering beneath a tree at an Indian spiritual retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a hermitage or community where Hindus gather for religious instruction.

clue.text: Young one on farm has broken leg in deep hole

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a pit is a deep hole

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A farm animal has broken its leg falling into a deep hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an injured animal, but 'broken' is the signal to rearrange and 'deep hole' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A piglet is a young pig, a baby animal found on a farm.

clue.text: Half of them getting very angry in Dubai?

indicators.note: taking half the word, here its second half

parts.note: irate means very angry

explanation.surface: Half of them getting furious in a Gulf city.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Dubai as an example of the answer rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the seven states of the United Arab Emirates, each ruled by an emir.

clue.text: Portuguese ventriloquist concealing affair

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them, keeping it out of sight

explanation.surface: An Iberian puppet-voicer keeping a love affair secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Affair looks romantic here but means an occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence or happening, as is an affair in the sense of 'a grand affair'.

clue.text: Taken illegally, as egg may be

definitions.meaning: first meaning: game that is ... is taken unlawfully
second meaning: an egg may be cooked by poaching in simmering water

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe the one word: unlawful hunting and a way of cooking eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Poached covers both stolen game or fish and food gently simmered in liquid.

clue.text: Singer caught in maelstrom occasionally

indicators.note: only now and then, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A vocalist trapped now and then in a whirlpool.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with the voice range below soprano.

clue.text: Permission to go

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as a noun is permission, as in 'by your ...'

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, permission to depart, but splits into a noun and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for consent granted and a verb meaning to depart.

clue.text: French heads welcoming a private conversation

indicators.note: letting something in, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: tete is French for head, so two heads give TETE TETE

explanation.surface: French leaders hosting a confidential talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Heads is plural, so it gives two French heads, TETE twice, with A between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tete-a-tete, literally head to head, is an intimate chat between two people.

clue.text: Husband out of danger? That's a nice surprise?

indicators.note: removed from, so that letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a threat is a danger

explanation.surface: A husband out of harm's way: what a pleasant surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is something unexpected that gives pleasure, a delight.
